issue_plan.name: Finish plumbing on configured repositories
issue_plan.summary: After all ten steps of #564 have merged, these three issues complete #566 and the remaining work in #452. First, invariant init drafts repository configuration for a person to complete and commit; next, its generated CI gate checks the configured parts and ratified plans. Finally, the factory accepts plumbing on configured GitHub repositories and exercises the complete flow for Go, Python, TypeScript and a mixed monorepo. Checks and trust come from the committed base, changes to trusted files wait for a person, and repositories without configuration retain the existing unsupported response.

issues.title: Draft repository configuration with invariant init
issues.body:
Extend invariant init and internal/setup to draft .invariant/repository.json from the checkout so a person can review, complete and commit the repository's check configuration. This is the first of #566's three changes, formerly step 8 of #452, and starts only after all ten steps of #564 have merged. It builds on the version 1 contract in internal/repository and D-0301; it supplies discovery and drafting only. The following issue upgrades the generated gate, and external plumbing remains disabled until the final issue.

Discover Go modules and go.sum, Python pyproject.toml or requirements.txt and available dependency locks, and TypeScript package.json, scripts and lockfiles. Discover multiple parts, including nested parts and mixed-language monorepos. Exclude vendored dependencies, generated trees and installed environments such as node_modules and virtual environments. Keep discovery inside the checkout with safe, clean repository-relative paths. Discovery must execute no repository scripts, import no repository code and install nothing.

Draft each part's directory, language, digest-pinned toolchain, dependency inputs, lockfiles and the six command declarations: install, format, lint, build, test and test_one. Commands are argument arrays interpreted in the part directory, never shell text; test_one follows the existing native acceptance conventions. Discover declared current-state documents and root or nested agent rules from repository evidence, and express ownership and shared inputs using the existing contract. Use maintained digest-pinned toolchain defaults from internal/toolchain where compatible and known. A formatting check must fail on differences; do not claim that a command which merely prints differences is a working check.

Respect the existing dependency preparation and native acceptance support: Go modules, hash-locked pip requirements, supported npm package locks, and Go, pytest, Vitest or Jest test conventions. Discover other lock conventions as evidence but identify unsupported installation or ambiguous commands for manual completion rather than adding new package managers in this change. Never treat floating requirements as a lock, invent a command when discovery is inconclusive, or disguise an unresolved field as a reason a check does not apply. Clearly identify unresolved toolchain, lock, ownership or command fields, including when no project is detectable. Any draft with unresolved requirements must fail enabled-configuration validation until a person completes it; a fully resolved draft must satisfy the existing contract when committed.

Preserve init's existing workflow pinning and normal non-overwrite behavior. Leave an existing customized repository configuration intact and report it clearly; rerunning against identical generated output must be safe. Keep modeled-project setup working, including repositories with no detectable native project. Print guidance that a person reviews and commits the file on the base branch and must install a gate capable of the configured checks before plumbing can be enabled. Do not upgrade the gate template or enable intake in this issue.

Acceptance: add setup and CLI fixtures for Go, Python, TypeScript, a mixed monorepo, multiple supported lock conventions, discovered unsupported locks, missing locks, floating requirements, unknown commands, no detectable project and an edited existing configuration. Assert digest pinning or explicit unresolved output, valid paths and ownership, exclusion of dependency/generated/environment trees, no repository execution or installation, repeatability and non-overwrite behavior. Commit resolved and unresolved fixture drafts to prove the loader accepts only the complete ones. Preserve existing init and modeled-setup tests.

Keep SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md accurate for this step, explicitly retaining the external-intake limitation. Cite the decisions the change rests on. The factory PR cannot write decisions/: whoever merges it records its decision with invariant decisions decide before the next step, following AGENTS.md and D-0122/D-0294.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Generate a CI gate for repository checks and ratified plans
issues.body:
Complete the external-repository gate generated by invariant init so invariant/gate enforces configured repository checks, native acceptance tests, scope and ratification. This is the second change in #566, formerly step 9 of #452. It follows configuration drafting and assumes #564's dependency preparation, sandbox execution, native plan, scope, trust and context work has merged. Keep external plumbing intake disabled until the next issue.

Add an invariant check-repository CLI entry point suitable for CI. Resolve configuration through internal/repository from the authoritative committed base, never from the candidate working tree or its edited repository.json. For a factory pull request, validate its ratified native plan and captured execution authority, select affected parts using the existing ownership rules and admitted regressions, prepare their locked dependencies and run declared format, lint, build and test commands plus the plan's pinned acceptance tests through the same sandbox and native adapters as factory builds. Preserve offline execution after dependency preparation, existing time and cleanup allowances, and failure reporting, including skipped or unstarted phases and their reasons. The command must return failure for a failed check or invalid authority, scope or pinned tests. Ordinary pull requests and push CI must also check configured repositories, running all parts when no reliable change selection is available. Absence of a repository contract preserves modeled-only operation; malformed configuration must not silently become a successful no-op.

Update internal/setup/gate.yml to invoke repository checks and make their failure fail invariant/gate. Retain scope checks for factory branches, with the issue derived from the branch, and extend ratification to .invariant/plans/issue-N.json records as well as modeled project manifests. Discover both independently so a repository containing only plans is checked. Guard empty lists so an empty modeled-only repository never invokes ratification with no arguments. Verify pinned acceptance sources and reject out-of-plan changes; editing or removing candidate configuration cannot weaken checks or bypass scope or ratification.

Preserve the full pinned Invariant revision, read-only workflow permissions, modeled verification, receipt and trace upload, and the invariant/gate job name. This changes the workflow template generated for other repositories, not Invariant's own CI workflow or gate behavior. Make the generated workflow usable with the preceding init draft after a person completes and commits it. Extend setup guidance and capability validation in internal/setup and the CLI integration so an older workflow with only the invariant/gate job name is insufficient for configured plumbing and receives an actionable upgrade message. Existing modeled-only setup must continue to work with its current gate requirements; do not overwrite customized workflows silently.

Acceptance: generated-workflow and CLI fixtures cover Go, Python, TypeScript and a mixed monorepo using real configuration loading, ownership selection, scope, ratification and sandbox orchestration with fake external processes. Exercise each configured check failing, missing or wrong plan ratification, changed pinned tests, out-of-plan edits, and candidate configuration edits attempting to skip or weaken checks. Prove plan-only ratification, the empty modeled-only guard, ordinary CI checks and the full-check fallback. Assert dependency preparation precedes offline native tests and that a confined factory change in one monorepo part does not run the untouched part's suite. Test rejection and upgrade guidance for an obsolete configured gate while retaining modeled-only compatibility, pinned revision, read-only permissions, modeled verification and receipt upload.

Keep SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md accurate for this step and explain the manual gate upgrade, without claiming external intake is enabled. This builds on D-0105, D-0301 and the native plan and execution decisions. Follow AGENTS.md: the factory PR cannot write decisions/, and whoever merges it records the decision with invariant decisions decide before the next step, under D-0122/D-0294.

issues.title: Enable configured plumbing and test the complete factory flow
issues.body:
Enable plumbing on configured GitHub repositories and verify the complete factory flow. This is the final change in #566, formerly step 10 of #452, after all of #564 and the configuration-drafting and generated-gate issues have merged. The committed repository contract, locked dependency preparation, native acceptance plans, sandbox, captured context, scope, trust and generated CI gate are prerequisites; this issue connects them to public factory intake and removes D-0121's temporary repository restriction.

Replace the gitdek/invariant-only eligibility check in internal/factory/plumbing.go and factory.go. An external GitHub repository may take plumbing only with a valid .invariant/repository.json committed on its authoritative base and a gate supporting the preceding issue's repository, scope and ratification checks. Do not force req.Language to Go: use the captured parts and existing native framework support for Go, Python, TypeScript and mixed repositories. Configuration found only on an issue branch, in an uncommitted checkout or in a builder workspace cannot enable plumbing.

Resolve and pass one authoritative repository context through planning and revisions, hash ratification, building, fallback and repairs, read-only review, scope and publication. Reuse the captured snapshot, commands, dependencies, rules, documents, native test identities and trust policy supplied by the existing components; candidate files cannot replace them. Validate ratified execution authority and revalidate the committed base and required gate before readiness or merge. Preserve current compatible-base movement and checked-head merge behavior; removed or changed authority must stop the work for a person rather than silently select new checks.

For an external repository without a base configuration, retain the unsupported outcome and human-review label, with no agent run, proposal or build branch, including after revisions and repeated polls. Explain the now-available setup path in that response. Invalid configuration and obsolete or missing gate capabilities receive specific setup failures. Keep Invariant's built-in plumbing working without repository.json. Modeled-project builds, existing supported hosts and languages, ratification hashes and locks, and the proved protocol remain unchanged.

Preserve configured trust and publication rules: out-of-plan edits are refused, and changes to the repository contract, CI, agent rules and other captured trusted paths wait for a person. Trust derives from the base and actual changes, including deletions, never a plan's display metadata. Successful trusted builds remain drafts, including recovered and retried builds; ordinary in-scope builds can publish ready pull requests after successful checks and review. Workflow credential refusals retain the recorded build and produce a durable human handoff, with publication resumed only by the existing explicit retry flow after credentials are fixed.

Acceptance: add end-to-end Go, Python and TypeScript fixtures covering an issue's real planning check, hash ratification, real plumbing.Builder, native checks, review, scope and ready-PR publication. Follow internal/factory/review_repair_accept_test.go: replace agents, GitHub and container processes while exercising the real orchestration, rather than using a builder that returns success. Every fixture's pinned acceptance test must fail against its base and pass only after the build's change. Assert locked installation and cache reuse, network only during installation, and offline checks. Include a Go/TypeScript monorepo where only the touched part's suite runs. Exercise out-of-plan refusal, repository-file/CI/agent-rule human holds, retries and recovery, and a workflow-publication credential refusal without an automatic repeated write or rebuild. Cover missing configuration on initial intake and revision, malformed configuration, an obsolete gate, branch/workspace-only configuration, candidate attempts to weaken authority and a base configuration or gate change before merge.

Run the relevant existing Invariant plumbing, scope, ratification, setup and factory compatibility tests. Finish SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md with setup examples, the repository contract, native tests, captured trust, human holds and no-file behavior. Replace the current D-0121 limitation only now that it is removed. Follow AGENTS.md and D-0122/D-0294: the factory PR cannot write decisions/, so whoever merges it records the decision with invariant decisions decide before further work. Hosted operation, additional languages or hosts and decision-followup automation remain outside #452.
